newsitem.title: USA: Conn. comptroller sees bigger general fund surplus.
newsitem.headline: Conn. comptroller sees bigger general fund surplus.

text.p: Connecticut Comptroller Nancy Wyman on Thursday increased revenues would allow the state's general fund to run a surplus larger than previously expected, despite overspending on several accounts.

Wyman said general fund revenues were projected to be $325.8 million higher than budgeted, without including interyear transfers. Income tax collections are now expected to outstrip budget projections by nearly seven percent.
Wyman said in a letter to Gov. John Rowland that spending for the year ending June 30 was projected to be $182.9 million more than budgeted.
However, state income tax refunds will come in $64 million lower than previously estimated, she said.

Wyman projected the year-end surplus at $221.7 million, but added that if the legislature approves Rowland's plan to make $116.5 million in financial transfers between fiscal years, the surplus would drop to $107.2 million.
She said the figures augured well for biennial budget negotiations between the legislature and the governor.
"The good news is that the state is gaining jobs, wages are increasing, financial markets are fundamentally sound, and the national economy is continuing its solid growth," she said.

"The strong revenue performance of this past month signals future growth and increases the likelihood that the governor and the legislature will be able to reach a budget agreement that provides much-needed tax relief while maintaining essential state services," Wyman said.

She said the governor was fortunate that increased spending was covered by increased revenues. Two-thirds of the excess spending was on Medicaid ($80.4 million), foster care for children ($23 million) and University of Connecticut operations ($9.1 million).

State tax refunds for the period ending April 15 were much lower than Wyman had projected, most likely because fewer people took advantage of the new $100 property tax credit than she had expected, she said.
